messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene with three adult friends in a kitchen after dinner. Keep each character involved naturally, but do not make everyone speak in a perfect rotation. One person can interrupt another, two can talk while the third does something else, and the conversation can briefly become one-on-one before returning to the group. Output only story prose.

Priya rinsed the last plate while Daniel dried it. Marcus was sitting on the counter, scrolling through his phone.

“You're not helping,” Daniel said.

“I’m providing moral support.”

“You've been providing it for twenty minutes.”

“It's a demanding role.”

Priya laughed. “Hand me the big pan.”

Daniel passed it over. Marcus finally looked up.

“Are we still going out tomorrow?”

“Depends,” Priya said. “What time?”

“Whenever.”

“That means nothing.”

Daniel stacked the plates. “He means whenever he wakes up.”

“I wake up early.”

“No, you don't.”

Marcus pointed at Priya. “Tell him.”

“I have known you for too long to support that argument.”

“Wow.”

Daniel grinned. “She's learning.”

Priya dried her hands and looked at Marcus. “What did you find, anyway?”

He turned the phone toward her. “That restaurant we went to last year opened another location.”

“Oh, the one with the terrible chairs?”

“The chairs were fine,” Daniel said.

“They were not.”

Marcus laughed. “I knew you'd remember.”

Priya shook her head and reached for the dish towel. “We'll pick somewhere else.”

“Fine,” Marcus said. “But I'm not choosing.”

Daniel looked at him. “You're never choosing.”

“That is leadership.”
